title: The Saviors by Bubba Weiler at Atlantic Theater Company #thesaviors #...
transcript: From the folks behind “well, I'll let you go” comes another movingly melancholy play. This one is about a pair of altar boys growing up in a small, rural community and the toll that self discovery takes when your whole life has been historically prescribed. As the two of them learn about themselves and the world around them, a lot of uncomfortable questions arise. In some ways, it's a classic story of religious trauma, but while that theme is massive, this play is pretty restrained and small in scope. This enables us to focus on these characters specifically, watching them grapple with the fact that the world is not as black or white as the binary concepts they've been raised on, and what that does to the psyche at such an impressionable age. I was charmed by the actors’ performances, and I was warmed by this depiction of boys who are trying so earnestly to be good — especially considering the real-life backdrop of many young men being pulled into the manosphere. The two supporting characters in this play are a church mentor and a loner. They mostly serve as plot devices, but they have interesting backstories that I kinda wish there was more time to explore. If playwright Bubba Weiler sees this, I would love a prequel. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
